h1: The 6 Best Cordless Vacuums Under $200 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Cordless Vacuums Under $200: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six cordless stick vacuums that all sit under $200, ranked by listed battery run time and power for apartments and homes.
summary: The Uosogi Cordless Vacuum is our top pick for the longest listed run time at 70 minutes with a 650W rating. The JELLYPIG matches those numbers as a close second. The Levoit and Electrolux offer 50 minutes each, while the Hoover ONEPWR and Shark Pet are the name-brand options with shorter run times.
intro: Run time is the spec that decides whether a cordless vacuum replaces your corded one or becomes the thing you charge between every room. In this price range the listed minutes vary by almost double, and that gap tells you more than any brand name.

Every vacuum here sits within the $100-200 bracket. We reviewed their listed run times and power ratings and ranked six. The listings say little else, so we say plainly where a pick wins only on a number.

products.name: Uosogi Cordless Vacuum Cleaner
products.verdict: The longest listed run time here, 70 minutes, with 650W.
products.description:
The Uosogi lists a 70 minute run time and a 650W motor rating in a cordless design.

It leads because no other vacuum in this bracket lists more minutes, and it pairs them with the top wattage figure. The tradeoff against the name brands is that the listing is thin on features beyond those two numbers.

It is a good fit for larger apartments where you vacuum several rooms in one go. Check what attachments are in the box before you buy.
products.idealFor: Larger homes needing long run time.

products.name: JELLYPIG Cordless Vacuum Cleaner
products.verdict: Matches the 70 minute and 650W figures of the top pick.
products.description:
The JELLYPIG lists the same 70 minute run time and 650W rating as the Uosogi.

It sits second only because there is nothing to separate the two on paper, and the Uosogi takes the tiebreak on listing order. Either one beats the shorter-running pack below.

It works for anyone who sees it at a lower price than the Uosogi. The listing reveals little beyond the two numbers.
products.idealFor: Shoppers comparing it against the Uosogi on price.

products.name: Levoit Cordless Vacuum Cleaner
products.verdict: A named brand with a listed 50 minute run time.
products.description:
The Levoit Cordless Vacuum lists a 50 minute run time on a cordless body.

Third place reflects 20 fewer minutes than the 70-minute pair, partly offset by the better-known maker. It is level with the Electrolux below on run time.

It suits a one or two bedroom home. The wattage is not given in the listing, so compare suction by reading owner feedback.

products.name: Electrolux WellQ7 Cordless 2-in-1 Vacuum with High Suction Power and
products.description:
The Electrolux WellQ7 is a cordless 2-in-1 vacuum with a listed 50 minute run time.

It ties the Levoit on minutes and ranks below it only because the Levoit's listing is simpler. The 2-in-1 design is the difference that matters.

It is for buyers who want a handheld option as well. Confirm in the listing how the conversion works.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting a handheld as well.

products.name: Hoover ONEPWR WindTunnel Emerge Cordless Stick Vacuum
products.verdict: A ONEPWR stick vacuum with a listed 45 minutes.
products.description:
The Hoover ONEPWR WindTunnel Emerge is a cordless stick vacuum with a listed 45 minute run time.

It ranks fifth for giving up 5 minutes to the Levoit and Electrolux. Its ONEPWR name hints at a shared battery system, though the listing here does not spell it out.

It suits Hoover loyalists. Verify battery sharing in the full listing.
products.skipIf: You want the longest run time.

products.name: Shark Pet Cordless Stick Vacuum
products.verdict: A name-brand pet stick vacuum with 40 minutes listed.
products.description:
The Shark Pet is a cordless stick vacuum with a listed 40 minute run time.

It ranks last because 40 minutes is the shortest run time in this ranking, though the Shark name and pet focus have a following.

It works for small spaces and quick cleanups. The listing gives no wattage, so rely on the brand reputation with care.
products.skipIf: You clean a large home in one go.

whatMatters.detail: Run time is how many minutes the battery lasts, usually at the lowest power mode. A short run time means stopping mid-clean. Find the minutes figure in the title or bullets and match it to your home size.
Watts describe motor input, which loosely relates to suction. A higher number can mean stronger pickup, but it is not a full measure. Look for it in the listing, and note when it is missing.
A 2-in-1 splits into a handheld for stairs and upholstery. It is more versatile but may be heavier. Check how the conversion works in the listing.
Some brands share batteries across tools. This lowers cost if you own other tools from that line. Check whether the battery is included.
Several listings omit wattage or attachments. You cannot compare what is missing. Read the full listing before you buy.

faq.q: Does the listed run time match real use?
faq.a: Listed run time is usually for the lowest setting, so expect less at full power.
Buying on brand without checking minutes. Here the range is 40 to 70.

faq.q: Is the Uosogi worth it over Shark?
faq.a: On paper yes for run time, though Shark has a stronger brand.
Dock or plug per the manual. Charge fully before first use.

faq.q: How do I maintain a cordless vacuum?
faq.a: Empty the bin and clean the filter regularly.

faq.q: Do all of these cost under $200?
faq.a: All sit in the $100-200 bucket in our data, but check the live price.

finalTake: The Uosogi is the pick for the most listed minutes, with the JELLYPIG a near twin. Levoit is the sensible name-brand middle, and the Shark Pet suits small spaces. Choose by minutes first.
